question: What is the primary objective of the National Single Window System (NSWS) portal?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Single-point industrial clearance system**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Single Window System (NSWS)** is an initiative by the **Government of India** to provide a **single-point access to clearances and approvals** required for businesses in India.
 
• It is designed to promote the **‘Ease of Doing Business’** by reducing the complexities and delays in obtaining approvals and registrations for industrial and commercial activities.
 
• The NSWS serves as a **digital platform** that integrates the approval processes of various central and state departments, making it a **one-stop solution** for industries seeking to set up or expand their businesses.
 
• This platform helps industries save time and resources by eliminating the need to approach multiple authorities separately for approvals. *Hence, the NSWS acts as a single-point industrial clearance system.*
 
• The system is particularly aimed at fostering **investment and industrial growth** by ensuring a seamless approval process, thereby making India an attractive destination for domestic and global investors.
 
• By offering transparency, accountability, and a time-bound approval mechanism, the NSWS is a significant step toward **streamlining governance** and improving the ease of doing business in India.
 
• The portal was launched as part of the **Digital India initiative** and aligns with the government’s vision to create a business-friendly environment across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of the NSWS:**

 
 
• **Integrated digital platform:** The NSWS integrates approval processes from multiple central ministries and state governments, providing a **centralized mechanism** for industrial clearances.
 
• **Transparent and accountable:** The system is designed to ensure **real-time tracking of applications**, reducing chances of corruption and delays.
 
• **Time-bound approvals:** The NSWS ensures that businesses receive their approvals in a **time-bound manner**, enhancing the ease of doing business.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the NSWS:**
 
 
• To provide a **single-window clearance** mechanism for businesses, improving the efficiency and effectiveness of government services.
 
• To promote **industrial development** and attract **foreign direct investments (FDI)** by simplifying the approval process.
 
• To ensure **policy alignment** and coordination among different departments and ministries involved in the approval process.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Successful Implementation:**
 
 
• **States' participation:** Many states have adopted the NSWS platform, integrating their own single-window clearance systems with the central platform.
 
• **Case studies:** Industrial projects in states like **Gujarat** and **Karnataka** have benefitted from faster approvals and reduced delays due to the adoption of NSWS.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**

 
 
• The NSWS is not related to **pension tracking for workers**, which is managed under schemes like the **Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)** or **Atal Pension Yojana**.
 
• It is not linked to **school enrollment monitoring**, which is handled by the **Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE)** or other education initiatives.
 
• The NSWS does not deal with **water testing management**, which is managed under programs like the **Jal Jeevan Mission** or **National Water Quality Monitoring Programme (NWQMP)**.
 
 
 
• **Impact of NSWS:**
 
 
• The platform has significantly contributed to India’s **ranking improvement** in the **Ease of Doing Business Index** published by the **World Bank**.
 
• The system enhances India's attractiveness as a global investment destination by creating a **business-friendly environment**.
